cards.fr: What three parts make up triple assessment of a breast lump?
cards.bk: Clinical examination, breast imaging and tissue diagnosis by image-guided core biopsy.

cards.fr: Why are both breasts imaged when breast cancer is suspected?
cards.bk: Up to 3% of patients have hidden cancer in the other breast.

cards.fr: Which adhesion protein is lost in invasive lobular carcinoma?
cards.bk: E-cadherin. Lobular cancer is usually ER positive and HER2 negative.

cards.fr: Which breast cancer subtype lacks ER, PR and HER2?
cards.bk: Triple-negative cancer. It relies on chemotherapy, with immunotherapy added, and carries a poorer prognosis.

cards.fr: What T category is a breast tumour that reaches the chest wall or skin?
cards.bk: T4, whatever its size. Inflammatory breast cancer is staged T4d.

cards.fr: How is the axilla staged when the nodes are clinically negative?
cards.bk: Sentinel lymph node biopsy. Nodes proven to be involved get axillary clearance instead.

cards.fr: Which targeted antibody treats HER2-positive breast cancer, and what must be monitored?
cards.bk: Trastuzumab, often with pertuzumab and chemotherapy. The LVEF is monitored.

cards.fr: Paget disease of the nipple looks like eczema of the nipple and areola but sits over {{DCIS or an invasive cancer}}.
cards.bk: It is not a simple dermatitis, so a persistent nipple change needs assessment for cancer.

cards.fr: After mastectomy, {{four or more}} positive axillary nodes make chest wall and nodal radiotherapy mandatory.
cards.bk: A node-negative tumour of 5 cm or less with clear margins needs none.

cards.fr: Name the T category each hidden label marks.

boxes.label: T2: over 2 cm, up to 5 cm
T4: chest wall or skin; T4d is inflammatory

cards.bk: Size sets T1 to T3. Reaching the chest wall or skin makes it T4 at any size.
